differences.title: 1. PRIMARY USE CASE
differences.leftDesc: Designed for transactional data persistence within applications, embedding a relational database directly into the executable for single-user or low-concurrency scenarios.
differences.rightDesc: Optimized for fast analytical queries on large datasets, performing complex aggregations and joins directly in memory without a separate server process.

differences.title: 2. QUERY OPTIMIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Uses a traditional C-based query optimizer suitable for general SQL operations, prioritizing correctness and transactional integrity for row-based operations.
differences.rightDesc: Employs vectorized query execution (SIMD), processing data in batches for significantly faster analytical computations and aggregations compared to row-by-row.

differences.title: 3. DATA FORMAT
differences.leftDesc: Stores the entire relational database, including tables, indexes, and metadata, within a single, portable disk file for ease of deployment.
differences.rightDesc: Internally organizes data in a columnar format, ideal for analytical queries that access only a subset of columns across many rows.

differences.title: 4. EXTENSIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: Supports user-defined functions (UDFs) written in C or other languages to extend its SQL capabilities for specific application logic needs.
differences.rightDesc: Allows custom data types, operators, and aggregates, enabling deep integration and specialized query capabilities for advanced analytical workflows.

differences.title: 5. CONCURRENCY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Utilizes file-level or row-level locking for managing concurrent access, which can become a bottleneck under high write contention.
differences.rightDesc: Implements a Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) system optimized for read-heavy analytical workloads, reducing blocking between readers and writers.

differences.title: 6. PERFORMANCE FOCUS
differences.leftDesc: Excels at fast, transactional INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations, making it suitable for OLTP-style application backends.
differences.rightDesc: Designed for blazing-fast SELECT queries and complex analytical aggregations, processing vast amounts of data efficiently for BI and data science.

differences.title: 7. DEPLOYMENT SCENARIO
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for mobile apps, desktop software, and simple web servers where a full database server is overkill and a single file is sufficient.
differences.rightDesc: Perfect for in-memory data processing, interactive data exploration in Python/R, and building analytical pipelines directly within applications.
